goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
goldens.reasoning: C1 says the same thing: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the UserModel argument.

goldens.comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points to the same problem. Because the method requires user != null, conditional passkey UI isn't set up on the initial login page, where the user is still null. C2 names UsernamePasswordForm instead of UsernameForm, but the root issue is the same.

candidates: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only available method is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). This won't compile.

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) currently requires user != null, which prevents UsernamePasswordForm from setting enableWebAuthnConditionalUI on the initial login screen (where context.getUser() is null) and on error challenges before the user is set, so themes/base/login/passkeys.ftl won't render the conditional passkeys form.
